finding.title: TeamViewer is installed on your computer
finding.description:
We found TeamViewer, a program that lets someone else control your screen from another computer. If you installed this for work or to help a friend, that is fine. However, if you do not remember installing it, it may have been added by someone else to watch your activity.

If you think a partner, ex, or family member installed this to monitor you, removing it can alert them. Talk to an advocate first (US National Domestic Violence Hotline: 1-800-799-7233, or text START to 88788).

What to do: If you did not install TeamViewer, open Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps, find TeamViewer, and select Uninstall.

remediation.title: Review installed remote-access tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, VNC, LogMeIn, RDP)

steps.title: Check if you use TeamViewer
steps.body:
1. Confirm: does anyone with legitimate reason to remotely support this
   machine (family IT help, a business you work with) use TeamViewer? If
   yes, no action needed.
2. If unrecognized or no longer needed, uninstall via Settings → Apps →
   Apps and features → search "TeamViewer" → Uninstall, then restart.

remediation.safety_note: Before you remove or turn anything off: if you think someone close to you set this up to watch you, removing it can alert them. Talk to an advocate first. In the US: National Domestic Violence Hotline, 1-800-799-7233, or text START to 88788.
